title: Team tools: the board updates itself; optional team check every ~6 h
problem:
Answer: half of all incidents (72 of 145) are team slips, not page bugs, and most come from agents copying facts the tools already have.

- The board learns about your answers late: 7 of your 19 answers today took over 10 min to show (median 9 min; the decision on the hero accent word proposal took 17 min, I-145).
- The lead missed that decision too: its listener filter drops proposal lines.
- Agents write about 575 board updates a day, roughly 5 % of one usage window (estimate).
- The lead writes about half of all output tokens, mostly coordination.
- 9 agents answered 'what slowed you today': hand-made chains of lock holds, reading each other's files, phone hand-offs, and copied scripts.

Full plan: research/architecture/team-ops-plan.md.

What you need to do: pick one option.
risk: All options change tools only through toolsmiths, one incident at a time, with tests. Nothing changes how pages are measured.

options.name: tools-first
options.label: Tools first, no new role
options.idea:
- Board: once you answer, 'waiting on you' disappears at once (from the event, not from the agent).
- One wake line for every event, so no listener can filter a decision out.
- Lock: run a chain of holds; reserve the phone for a promised user step.
- A read-only peer file reader; flaky-test reports joined, not filed four times.
- The desk answers status questions on a cheaper model; decisions still go to the lead.
options.looksSame: The pages look the same; rows just stay current.
options.risk: Medium for the lock changes (chain, phone reservation): fairness needs tests. Low for the rest (read-only views).
visualDiff: Board rows show 'you answered at 13:09Z; owner has not picked it up' in place of a stale 'waiting on you'

gain.what: Your answers shown late on the board (over 10 min)
gain.how: today's proposal/step answers vs the owner's next board write
status store history today; waits and measuring/testing come from events

live.none: A team process change: there is no page to try. The pictures show today and the option.

options.name: tools-and-check
options.label: Tools + a team check every ~6 h
options.idea:
- Everything in 'Tools first'.
- Agents log friction in one line when it happens (no extra turn).
- A short-lived checker on a cheaper model, every ~6 h or after each wave, reads that log, asks only the agents with no note, and hands the lead ready incident lines.
- It also re-measures board lag, lead load and minutes you waited on a stuck step, so you can see the trend.
options.looksSame: The pages look the same; an FYI thread per check.
options.risk: Costs a little every round; agents may ignore the friction log (the checker then asks them).
visualDiff: One short FYI thread per check (every ~6 h) with what it found

gain.what: Slips found before they become incidents
gain.how: one manual round today, 9 of 10 agents answered
~10 agent turns per round plus the checker

live.none: A team process change: there is no page to try. The pictures show today and the option.

options.name: minimal
options.label: Minimal: fix only what you saw
options.idea:
- Board: once you answer, 'waiting on you' disappears at once.
- One wake line for every event, so the lead never misses a decision.
- The router ignores agents whose listener stopped (I-137).
- Everything else stays as today.
options.risk: Lowest. Lock chains, phone hand-offs and double work stay as they are.
visualDiff: Same as 'Tools first' for the board; nothing else changes

gain.what: Your answers shown late on the board (over 10 min)

live.none: A team process change: there is no page to try. The pictures show today and the option.

recommended.why: The tools fix what you saw. The check finds the next slips early: today's one manual round found 6 items no incident had, for about 2-3 % of a window.
